description:
FILED s532b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-06) while fixing #4163, whose filing guessed the opposite ("`package Q; our @INC` is @main::INC") -- perl 5.40.3 says otherwise.  PRE-EXISTING (59317afd the same).  LOW: rare, and a silent wrong only for a program that relies on it.

    perl -e 'package Q; our @INC; print \@INC == \@main::INC ? "same\n" : "diff\n";
             our %ENV; print \%ENV == \%main::ENV ? "esame\n" : "ediff\n";
             package R; print \@INC == \@main::INC ? "rsame\n" : "rdiff\n";'
    perl: diff / ediff / rdiff        (the alias stays in scope across `package R`)
    scratch/s532b/pr/p4163c.pl: `package Q; our @INC; print scalar(@INC) > 0 ? "inc-is-main" : "inc-empty"` -> perl inc-empty, PCL inc-is-main (same for %ENV).

perl: `our` adds a pad entry whose OURSTASH is PL_curstash and fetches the glob QUALIFIED with it (op.c / pad.c), so S_find_default_stash's forced-main list never applies.  An unqualified `@INC` with no `our` in scope is still @main::INC (that half is right in PCL).  Where: the `our` declaration's home in Parser2 (`_lower_our_decl`) and the binder's `our` record (Pl/Binder.pm's %SPECIAL_MAIN arm, ~line 653 -- s533d's region at the time of filing): an `our` binding of a forced-main name must home in the declaring package, and the uses it covers read that package's variable.  Probe: the three lines above + `our $_` (a lexical-ish special -- perl 5.40: `our $_` is allowed and is $main::_? probe it) + a sub reading the alias.
subject: `package Q; our @INC;` (and `our %ENV`, `our @ARGV` ...) names the CURRENT package's variable in perl -- @Q::INC, empty -- but PCL aliases @main::INC: `our` bypasses gv.c's forced-main rule because it qualifies explicitly
